classes.name: NullLogger
classes.description: No-op logger implementation. Used when no logger is configured in the application. All methods do nothing - safe for libraries to call without checking.

functions.name: getLogger
functions.description:
Get the configured logger or NullLogger if none configured.

Libraries should use this to get a logger instance. If the application hasn't configured logging, returns NullLogger (no-op).

jsdoctags.comment:
Library usage:

Example :
import { getLogger } from '@cocoar/logging-abstractions';

export class MyLibraryClass {
private logger = getLogger('MyLibraryClass');

doWork() {
this.logger.debug('Working...');
}
}

functions.name: getLoggerFor
functions.description:
Get a logger with source context extracted from class, instance, or string.

This is a convenience method that accepts:

  • String: Used as-is
  • Class constructor: Extracts class name
  • Class instance: Extracts class name from constructor
  • Plain object: Extracts "Object" (not useful, but won't crash)

jsdoctags.comment: • String, class constructor, or instance to extract source name from

Class source:

Example :
class MyService {}
const logger = getLoggerFor(MyService);  // source: 'MyService'

Instance source:

Example :
class MyComponent {
private logger = getLoggerFor(this);  // source: 'MyComponent'
}
true if logger is configured, false if using NullLogger
